'''Marston Donald Edward Conder''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|ONZM}} (born 9 September 1955) is a New Zealand mathematician, a <!-- "distinguished professor" is the full job title --> distinguished professor of mathematics at [[Auckland University]],<ref name="dir">[http://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/Directory/jahia/staff-profile-jahia.php?upi=mcon007 Staff directory listing entry], Auckland U. Mathematics, retrieved 22 January 2013.</ref> and the former co-director of the New Zealand Institute of Mathematics and its Applications. His main research interests are in [[combinatorial group theory]], [[graph theory]], and their connections with each other.

==Education and career==
Conder was born in [[Hamilton, New Zealand]], and studied at [[Matamata College]].<ref name="cf">[http://www.massey.ac.nz/~wwifs/mathnews/centrefolds/70/Aug1997.shtml Centrefold: Marston Conder] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054111/http://www.massey.ac.nz/~wwifs/mathnews/centrefolds/70/Aug1997.shtml |date=4 March 2016 }}, NZMS Newsletter 70, August 1997, retrieved 22 January 2013.</ref> He earned a master's degree in social science from [[Waikato University]] in 1977, and a doctorate from [[Oxford University]] in 1980 under the supervision of [[Graham Higman]].<ref name="cf"/><ref name="rsnz">[http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/current-fellows/?mde-conder RSNZ member profile], retrieved 22 January 2013.</ref><ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Marston Donald Edward Conder|id=26492}}</ref> He served as president of the New Zealand Mathematical Society from 1993 to 1995,<ref name="rsnz"/> and as president of the Academy of the Royal Society of New Zealand from 2006 to 2008. In 2011 he was selected as the inaugural Maclaurin Lecturer, as part of a reciprocal exchange between the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]] and the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.voxy.co.nz/national/mathematician-receives-joint-nz-us-honour/5/100070 Mathematician receives joint NZ-US honour] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150122233213/http://www.voxy.co.nz/national/mathematician-receives-joint-nz-us-honour/5/100070 |date=22 January 2015 }}, Voxy.co.nz, 1 September 2011, retrieved 22 January 2013.</ref>

==Recognition==
Conder is a fellow of the New Zealand Mathematical Society and of the [[Royal Society Te Apārangi]],<ref name="rsnz"/> and in 2012 became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 21 January 2013.</ref> He was named a distinguished alumnus of Waikato University for 2013.<ref>[http://alumni.waikato.ac.nz/news/university-of-waikato-celebrates-distinguished-alumni University of Waikato celebrates Distinguished Alumni for 2013], retrieved 7 December 2016.</ref> In 2011 he was awarded a [[James Cook Research Fellowship]] for research on symmetry of discrete structures.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Search James Cook Fellowship awards 1996–2017 |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/funds-and-opportunities/james-cook-research-fellowship/james-cook-research-fellowships-recipients/search-james-cook-fellowship-awards/ |access-date=2023-10-27 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Profile: Marston Conder |url=https://profiles.auckland.ac.nz/m-conder/professional |access-date=2023-10-27 |website=profiles.auckland.ac.nz}}</ref>

In March 2021 it was announced that Conder has been awarded the 2020 Euler Medal by the [[Institute of Combinatorics and its Applications]]<ref>{{cite news|title=2020 Euler Medal|url=https://www.auckland.ac.nz/en/news/2021/03/11/mathematician-wins-international-prize.html|publisher=The University of Auckland|accessdate=12 March 2021}}</ref> for his "many distinguished contributions to combinatorics over the last 40 years."

In 2014 the Royal Society Te Apārangi awarded Conder the [[Hector Medal]], and in 2018 the Jones Medal, named after [[Vaughan Jones]], "for his internationally renowned research on symmetry and chirality in discrete structures, and his exemplary leadership and service in the New Zealand mathematical sciences community".<ref>{{cite news|title=2018 Jones Medal: Symmetry and open questions|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/medals-and-awards/medals-and-awards-news/2018-jones-medal-symmetry-and-open-questions/|publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand|accessdate=31 May 2020}}</ref>
In the [[2020 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)| 2020 Birthday Honours]], he was appointed an Officer of the [[New Zealand Order of Merit]] (ONZM) for services to mathematics.<ref>{{cite news |title=Queen's Birthday Honours: The full list |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12336181 |accessdate=1 June 2020 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=1 June 2020}}</ref>
